summary: Seijun Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from circa 1977 to 1985. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University around 2002.

Seijun Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University from circa 1951 to 1955. He held a post at Taisho University from circa 1980 to 2003 and headed the Ishigami Zen'nō Kyōju Koki Kinen Ronbunshū Kankōkai around 2001.

Seikaku Hirata was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (circa 1946–1950) under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu and Bokuo Seki. He served on the faculty at Hanazono University from circa 1954 to 1995.

Specializing in linguistics and other fields, Sein Tin was educated at Basic Education High School No. 9 Mawlamyine, the University of Rangoon (~1920–1923), and Christ Church, Oxford (1924–1927), where he studied under Pe Maung Tin.

Seiran Ouchi worked in Buddhist and religious studies, founding Hoshi Sodan in 1874 and Meikyo Shinshi in 1875. He served as a lecturer at Nishi Hongan-ji and was president of Toyo University from 1914 to 1918.

Seiren Matsunami worked in Indology and Buddhist studies, graduating from the University of Tokyo by 1930 and studying under Naoshiro Tsuji and Walther Schubring. He held posts at Kyushu University (attested 1965, 1979), Taisho University, and Rissho University.

Karashima studied at the University of Tokyo, Cambridge, and Peking University under mentors including von Hinüber and Ji Xianlin. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology, he served at the Eastern Institute and Soka University's IRIAB (~1996–2019).

Seishin Kato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University and Shingiyaha Daigakurin. He served as president of Buzan University, professor and president of Toyo University, and president of Taisho University.
Seitatsu Matsunami is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as an assistant at the University of Tokyo and as a professor at Taisho University, attested in 1992.

Yanagida studied at Hanazono, Otani, and Kyoto universities under Kaiten Nukariya and Shin'ichi Hisamatsu. He specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, holding long-term posts at Hanazono University, Kyoto University, the IRIZ, and Chubu University.

Semen Ivanovich Tyulyaev, an art historian and Indologist, studied at Moscow State University (~1922–1927). He worked at the State Museum of Oriental Art (1927–1958) and the Institute of Oriental Studies (1958–1961), and taught at several Moscow institutes.

Sempa Dorje is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Ram Shankar Tripathi. He served as a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, attested in 1977 and between 1990 and 1998.

Semën Gesselevič Rudin was an Indologist and linguist who completed his undergraduate and candidate studies at Saint Petersburg State University (1947–1952, ~1959–1968). He also held a post at Saint Petersburg State University beginning in 1955.

Sen Wang was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Peking University from circa 1931 to 1935 and served as a professor at Minzu University of China from circa 1952 to 1991.

Senarat Wijayasundara is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1999, he was attested as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and as a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.
Senarath Paranavitana worked in archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jean Philippe Vogel from circa 1930 to 1936 and held a post at Leiden University.

Senchu Murano was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1929–1933) and the University of Washington (~1934–1938). He later served as a professor at Rissho University, attested in 1972.

Sengaku Mayeda was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo and University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown. He held teaching posts at the University of Pennsylvania, the University of Tokyo, and Musashino University.

Senkyo Sakawa is a Buddhist studies and archaeology scholar who completed his studies at Rissho University by 1965. He served as a professor and later professor emeritus at Rissho University, and worked at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

Senmyo Naniwa is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University, studying under G. Sasaki, M. G. Dhadphale, J. R. Joshi, and P. V. Bapat. He held posts at Bukkyo University and Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
